riskBefore: Hash-only Windows verification still allowed transient payload substitution, while caller-selected Android tools/device claims, non-ZIP APKs, unbound runner versions, and path/URI/property-bearing JUnit could create false release evidence.
controlsAdded: Common release invocation, unique lane invocation, exact lane/source binding, matching final preflight, freshness, and duplicate rejection.

Canonical repository-contained Windows AppPath with no reparse traversal; every payload file is opened FileShare.Read, hashed from its leased handle, and retained through real process/UI/post-run verification.
A checked-in Android policy schema binds the current commit, Mr. X approval receipt, exact tool paths/hashes/versions, exact managed device identity, and exact E2E APK identity.

The checked-in policy template is intentionally unprovisioned; a real policy and all trusted files must live below ignored .secrets/android-lab, while synthetic policy requires an explicit contract-test switch and cannot pass release validation.
The wrapper independently queries trusted adb/device state, validates a real ZIP APK plus package/version/certificate, and treats caller paths/serial only as exact policy cross-checks.
Android runner result v3 binds policy, tool, APK, device, JUnit, invocation, cleanup, and counter claims.
Debug-only network.xpoint.deep.e2e physical test package while Release remains network.xpoint.deep.

Raw Android evidence is quarantined locally; JUnit rejects system output/errors, attachments, absolute Windows/Unix paths, URIs, sensitive properties/values, and text payloads before any allowlisted summary is emitted.
Strict zero-skip gate with machine-readable blocked, failed, and passed states.
Real Windows ARM64 process and UIA3 control interaction.
Debug-only generated bootstrap path with unchanged release no-stub and endpoint guards.
Sanitized failure evidence and removal of private transient run data.
Android absence is blocked evidence instead of a passing APK-build proxy.
residualRisks: Android application behavior is not yet executed because Mr. X has not provisioned an approved commit-bound protected policy, trusted real tools, and an authorized managed device.
The Windows package proves the Welcome flow only; cross-process message delivery remains a later package.
A production provider push wake is not proven by this package.
